newsitem.title: FRANCE: State to have minority Thomson stake-Strauus-Kahn.
newsitem.headline: State to have minority Thomson stake-Strauus-Kahn.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Wednesday that the French state's stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF was expected to drop to below 50 percent from 58 percent now, with new partners.
He told reporters at the French parliament that he hoped the opening up of the capital of Thomson-CSF could take place before the end of this year.
On Friday, the Socialist-led government cancelled the planned privatisation sale of the 58-percent stake which had been started by the previous government.

The conservatives had short-listed missiles to publishing group Lagardere Groupe and an association of electronics and engineering group Alcatel Alsthom and warplane maker Dassault Aviation for the stake.
"We want to keep an important role in the future of Thomson-CSF," Strauss-Kahn told reporters after a hearing behind closed doors of the National Assembly's defence commission.

"If you want to have an alliance with a partner it is difficult to keep around 50 percent. That is why the Prime Minister talked (on Friday) about a decisive stake and not a majority stake," the finance minister said.
He did not exclude that the state's stake could be brought down to a blocking minority of 33 percent. "It's a good solution but there are other possibilities. Nothing has been decided."
A final decision on the future of Thomson-CSF depends on Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, whose office has direct control over the sensitive negotiations.
Jospin's office said on Friday it would launch new guidelines for Thomson-CSF in a matter of weeks, which most newspapers interpreted as the end of August or the beginning of September.
